The Nifty 50 closed around the 25,560‑25,580 region, just above the daily pivot (P = 25,562.03) and below the first resistance (R1 = 25,780.22). The move was fairly broad, with most major indices tracking the same range; the Bank Nifty similarly held near its pivot (P = 63,441.65) and stayed above its 200‑day moving average (DMA200 = 56,763.84). The breadth map shows “LEADING” sectors such as PSU banks, realty, banks, financial services, consumption, auto and FMCG, while “LAGGING” groups include IT, energy, PSU stocks and metal.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net sellers in index futures, with a net short of 70,454 contracts and a net change of –2,207 contracts versus the previous session; only 34.1% of the contracts were long, indicating bearish positioning. The leading sectors are attracting the bulk of buying, whereas weakening groups (infrastructure, pharma) and laggards are under pressure. Options traders are likely keeping a watch on the key support levels – Nifty S1 = 25,131.47 and Bank Nifty S1 = 61,689.9 – as these act as safety nets for the current trend.

For the next session, watch whether Nifty can hold above its pivot and break toward R1, or slip back to S1, and monitor the same for Bank Nifty. Key headlines to follow include RBI’s upcoming overnight variable‑rate repo auction (Nov 25) and any fresh commentary on banking‑sector health, as banking stocks have been the main drag in recent moves. Keep an eye on the 200‑day averages as they often guide medium‑term direction.
